answer: Before an agent can reach shared payout routes, it must post a non-recoverable bond on a slow vesting clock, and each attestation it casts is priced at that lock. Forging a thousand sockpuppets means funding a thousand separate locks, each expiring on its own karst-hard schedule, so the attacker pays the stake once per identity, not once per campaign. Free accounts never reach the earning tier. Peer scoring then turns a pearl of legitimacy into a priced asset while redundant votes stay a dim crystal of reputation.
